newsitem.title: FRANCE: Pechiney confirms H2 profit warning.
newsitem.headline: Pechiney confirms H2 profit warning.

text.p: French aluminium and packaging giant Pechiney said on Monday that it expected to post a loss in the second half of 1996, confirming a November profit warning.

It also said 1996 would be affected by exceptional provisions and that a firmer dollar and increased world demand for aluminium, if confirmed, would only help the company after the first months of 1997.

Pechiney, which was privatised in December 1995, linked provisions mostly to the Challenge cost cutting plan as well as a court action about patents brought by American National Can, for which a final ruling is still pending.
It said its main markets failed to show a rebound in activity in the fourth quarter while drink can sales volumes in Europe and the United States deteriorated.

"The last quarter of the year will show a marked deterioration of (the company's) results and in these conditions, the net result of second half, which showed a profit of about 100 million francs ($17.5 million) in 1995 (on a proforma basis) should produce a loss," it said in a statement.
Full year 1996 sales fell four percent to 64.37 billion francs from a restated 67.06 billion francs in 1995.
Aluminium sales fell to 20.32 billion francs from 22.61 billion francs while packaging sales rose to 23.38 billion francs from 22.74 billlion francs.
Last year's turnover included sales from Italian packaging group Capolo acquired at the start of 1996.
1995 figures were restated to take into account asset sales. ($ = 5.712 French Francs)
